title: Cardano gets custom USD stablecoins, but minus the customers — What should you know?
summary: Brale's launch connects Cardano to 30 blockchains, but no issuers have been named yet.
content: Brale has launched custom USD stablecoins on the Cardano network, connecting the blockchain to thirty other networks. However, the launch currently lacks specific issuers or customers. This development expands Cardano's cross-chain capabilities, though its practical adoption and usage will depend on future stablecoin issuers joining the platform.
content_ta: Brale நிறுவனம் Cardano நெட்வொர்க்கில் தனிப்பயன் USD stablecoins-ஐ அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் இந்த பிளாக்செயின் முப்பது பிற நெட்வொர்க்குகளுடன் இணைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. இருப்பினும், இந்த தொடக்கக் கட்டத்தில் குறிப்பிட்ட issuers அல்லது வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் யாரும் இன்னும் பெயரிடப்படவில்லை. இந்த வளர்ச்சி Cardano-வின் குறுக்கு-சங்கிலி திறன்களை விரிவுபடுத்துகிறது.

title: LayerZero adds Samsung Card, Kakao Pay, ZAN as validators for upcoming Zero blockchain
summary: Zero uses ZK proofs to separate execution from verification, removing a layer of redundancy by leaving validators to only verify the proofs.
content: LayerZero has integrated major financial and tech brands, including Samsung Card, Kakao Pay, and ZAN, as validators for its upcoming Zero blockchain. The Zero network utilizes zero-knowledge proofs to separate transaction execution from verification. This approach eliminates redundancy by allowing validators to focus exclusively on verifying the cryptographic proofs.
content_ta: வரவிருக்கும் தனது Zero blockchain-க்கான வேலிடேட்டர்களாக Samsung Card, Kakao Pay மற்றும் ZAN போன்ற முக்கிய நிறுவனங்களை LayerZero சேர்த்துள்ளது. Zero நெட்வொர்க் ஆனது பரிவர்த்தனை நிறைவேற்றுதலை சரிபார்ப்பிலிருந்து பிரிக்க ZK proofs-ஐப் பயன்படுத்துகிறது. வேலிடேட்டர்கள் சரிபார்ப்பு பணிகளில் மட்டும் கவனம் செலுத்த அனுமதிக்கிறது.

title: Lido tightens Ethereum staking penalties as operators gain access to larger validators
summary:
A March slashing involving six validators shows why Lido sought wider authority and when recovery could depend on future rewards or bond top-ups.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: Lido has increased Ethereum staking penalties as node operators gain access to larger validators. A recent slashing incident involving multiple validators highlighted the need for wider authority, as the platform addresses recovery mechanisms tied to future rewards and bond top-ups.
content_ta: Ethereum staking-ல் operator-கள் பெரிய validator-களை அணுகுவதால், Lido தண்டனைகளைக் கடுமையாக்கியுள்ளது. சமீபத்திய slashing சம்பவம் பல validator-களை பாதித்ததைத் தொடர்ந்து, எதிர்கால rewards மற்றும் bond top-up-களை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டு மீட்பு நடவடிக்கைகளை மேற்கொள்ள Lido அதிகாரம் கோரியுள்ளது.

title: Bitcoin Lightning operators could recover stuck payments even after losing channel data
summary:
The 26.12 release candidate can help recover eligible funds after channel data loss if the operator still has key records and can get help from the peer.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: A new release candidate for Bitcoin Lightning nodes, version 26.12, introduces a mechanism to recover stuck payments following a loss of channel data. This feature allows node operators to potentially restore funds if they possess specific key records and coordinate with their peer. This development addresses a significant vulnerability for Lightning Network users, offering a path to recover assets that were previously considered permanently inaccessible after local data corruption.
content_ta: Bitcoin Lightning nodes-ன் புதிய பதிப்பான 26.12, சேனல் டேட்டா இழப்பு ஏற்பட்டாலும் சிக்கியுள்ள பணத்தை மீட்டெடுக்கும் வசதியை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. நோட் ஆபரேட்டர்கள் தங்களின் முக்கிய ரெக்கார்டுகளை வைத்திருந்து, மற்றொறு பயனரின் உதவியைப் பெறுவதன் மூலம் நிதியை மீட்டெடுக்க முடியும். இந்த மேம்பாடு, மின்னல் நெட்வொர்க் (Lightning Network) பயனர்களுக்கு ஒரு முக்கிய தீர்வாக அமையும், ஏனெனில் முன்னதாக இத்தகைய டேட்டா இழப்பினால் நிதி நிரந்தரமாக முடக்கப்படும் சூழல் இருந்தது.

title: Bitcoin ETFs shed $4 billion — How did one fund hide the cracks before leading the exit?
summary: If one fund carries 84% of the exits, what exactly is the industry headline measuring?
content: Bitcoin ETFs have reported $4 billion in outflows, but market data reveals a skewed picture. One single fund is responsible for 84% of these withdrawals, raising questions about whether aggregate headlines accurately reflect the broader industry sentiment. While the massive exit from this specific fund dominates the narrative, the rest of the sector shows a significantly different trend, suggesting the headline figure may not represent the overall health of Bitcoin investment products.
content_ta: Bitcoin ETF-களில் இருந்து $4 பில்லியன் வெளியேறியுள்ளதாக தகவல்கள் தெரிவிக்கின்றன. ஆனால், இதில் 84 சதவீத வெளியேற்றம் ஒரே ஒரு ஃபண்டினால் மட்டுமே நடந்துள்ளது. ஒட்டுமொத்த சந்தையின் போக்கை இந்த ஒரு ஃபண்டின் தரவுகள் தவறாக சித்தரிக்கிறதா என்ற கேள்வி எழுந்துள்ளது. ஒட்டுமொத்த முதலீட்டுச் சந்தையின் உண்மையான நிலையை, இந்த தலைப்புச் செய்திகள் பிரதிபலிக்கிறதா அல்லது ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட ஃபண்டின் செயல்பாட்டை மட்டும் பெரிதுபடுத்துகிறதா என்பது தற்போது விவாதமாகியுள்ளது.

title: Coinbase CEO on the Anthropic and SpaceX IPOs: Who Actually Made the Money?
summary:
Anthropic and SpaceX trade below their IPO prices. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong says private backers took the gains.
The post Coinbase CEO on the Anthropic and SpaceX IPOs: Who Actually Made the Money? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong recently discussed the performance of high-profile companies like Anthropic and SpaceX following their public offerings. He highlighted that these firms are currently trading below their initial public offering prices. Armstrong argues that individual private backers, rather than public investors, have secured the majority of the financial gains from these ventures, raising concerns about the structure of market entry for retail participants.
content_ta: Anthropic மற்றும் SpaceX போன்ற நிறுவனங்களின் பங்குகள், சந்தையில் அறிமுகப்படுத்தப்பட்ட பிறகு, அவற்றின் ஆரம்ப விலையை விட குறைவான விலையிலேயே வர்த்தகமாகி வருவதாக Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong தெரிவித்துள்ளார். இந்த நிறுவனங்களின் ஆரம்ப முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மட்டுமே அதிக லாபம் ஈட்டியுள்ளதாகவும், பொது முதலீட்டாளர்களுக்கு பெரிய அளவில் பலன் கிடைக்கவில்லை என்றும் அவர் சுட்டிக்காட்டியுள்ளார்.

title: Bank of Korea Rate Hike Meets KOSPI Struggles: Can Chips Carry Korea?
summary:
The Bank of Korea rate hike to 3.25% meets a KOSPI about 48% below its June peak. Can chip exports carry Korea?
The post Bank of Korea Rate Hike Meets KOSPI Struggles: Can Chips Carry Korea? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: The Bank of Korea has increased its interest rate to 3.25%, a move occurring while the KOSPI index remains significantly lower than its June peak. Analysts are now closely monitoring whether the country's semiconductor export sector can provide enough economic momentum to overcome these ongoing market challenges. The ability of the chip industry to sustain Korea's broader financial recovery remains a central question for investors during this period of monetary tightening.
content_ta: Bank of Korea தனது வட்டி விகிதத்தை 3.25% ஆக உயர்த்தியுள்ளது. KOSPI குறியீடானது அதன் ஜூன் மாத உச்சத்திலிருந்து சரிந்த நிலையில் இருக்கும் சூழலில் இந்த நடவடிக்கை எடுக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. தென்கொரியாவின் குறைக்கடத்தி (semiconductor) ஏற்றுமதித் துறை, தற்போதைய சந்தை சவால்களைச் சமாளித்து பொருளாதார வளர்ச்சிக்கு உதவுமா என்பதை ஆய்வாளர்கள் கவனித்து வருகின்றனர். பணவியல் கொள்கை இறுக்கமாக்கப்பட்டுள்ள இந்த காலகட்டத்தில், சிப் தொழில்துறையின் செயல்பாடே கொரியாவின் பொருளாதார மீட்சிக்கு முக்கிய காரணியாக இருக்கும்.

title: CertiK Finds 38 Hidden AI Bugs That Could Cost the Industry Millions
summary:
Researchers at CertiK and Columbia University have discovered 38 bugs in software that performs some of the most fundamental calculations behind modern AI.  Among them are two bugs in DeepSeek’s DeepGEMM library and 23 in FlashAttention, a widely used technology that makes AI models run faster. One of these bugs went undetected through 17,760 runs
The post CertiK Finds 38 Hidden AI Bugs That Could Cost the Industry Millions appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Researchers from CertiK and Columbia University have identified 38 critical software bugs embedded within the foundations of modern AI technology. The flaws, found in widely used libraries such as DeepSeek’s DeepGEMM and FlashAttention, could lead to significant financial risks for the industry. Some of these vulnerabilities remained undetected despite thousands of rigorous testing cycles, highlighting a pressing need for enhanced security measures in the rapidly evolving artificial intelligence landscape.
content_ta: CertiK மற்றும் Columbia University ஆராய்ச்சியாளர்கள் இணைந்து நவீன AI தொழில்நுட்பத்தின் அடிப்படையான மென்பொருட்களில் 38 முக்கிய பிழைகளைக் கண்டறிந்துள்ளனர். DeepSeek நிறுவனத்தின் DeepGEMM மற்றும் FlashAttention போன்ற பரவலாகப் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் தொழில்நுட்பங்களில் இந்த பிழைகள் கண்டறியப்பட்டுள்ளன. இதனால் தொழில்துறைக்கு பெரும் நிதி இழப்பு ஏற்படும் அபாயம் உள்ளது. ஆயிரக்கணக்கான சோதனைகளுக்குப் பிறகும் சில பிழைகள் கண்டறியப்படாமல் இருந்திருப்பது, AI தொழில்நுட்பத்தின் பாதுகாப்பில் அதிக கவனம் செலுத்த வேண்டியதன் அவசியத்தை வலியுறுத்துகிறது.

title: Tech Stocks Stall Into Thanksgiving: Will the AI Rebound Return?
summary:
Tech stocks stall into Thanksgiving as Nvidia slips 4% and inflation fears return, leaving AI-linked shares under pressure.
The post Tech Stocks Stall Into Thanksgiving: Will the AI Rebound Return? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Technology stocks experienced a slowdown heading into the Thanksgiving holiday as Nvidia shares declined by four percent. Renewed concerns regarding inflation have impacted investor sentiment, putting significant pressure on various AI-linked equities. Analysts remain cautious about whether the recent momentum in artificial intelligence stocks will return as market volatility persists during the holiday period.
content_ta: Thanksgiving விடுமுறையை முன்னிட்டு தொழில்நுட்பப் பங்குகளின் வர்த்தகம் மந்தமடைந்துள்ளது. குறிப்பாக, Nvidia பங்குகளின் மதிப்பு நான்கு சதவீதம் சரிந்துள்ளதால் முதலீட்டாளர்கள் கவலையடைந்துள்ளனர். பணவீக்கம் குறித்த அச்சம் மீண்டும் எழுந்துள்ளதால், AI தொடர்பான நிறுவனங்களின் பங்குகள் அழுத்தத்தைச் சந்தித்து வருகின்றன. விடுமுறை காலத்தில் சந்தையில் நிலவும் இந்த ஏற்ற இறக்கம், AI பங்குகளின் மீட்சியைப் பாதிக்குமா என்ற எதிர்பார்ப்பு எழுந்துள்ளது.

title: Apple Stock Defies AI Selloff: Is It the Market's Safe Haven?
summary:
Apple stock is up 30.61% in 2026 while Nvidia falls 21.35%. See how low AI capex and a Gemini deal shaped the gap.
The post Apple Stock Defies AI Selloff: Is It the Market's Safe Haven? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Apple stock has demonstrated resilience amidst a broader market decline in AI-related shares. While competitors like Nvidia have seen significant losses in 2026, Apple has experienced growth. Analysts attribute this diverging performance to the company's strategic focus on capital expenditure and a notable deal involving Gemini. These factors have positioned Apple as a potential safe haven for investors during a period of sector-wide volatility.
content_ta: AI சார்ந்த நிறுவனங்களின் பங்குகள் சந்தையில் சரிவைச் சந்தித்து வரும் வேளையில், Apple நிறுவனத்தின் பங்குகள் நல்ல வளர்ச்சியைப் பதிவு செய்துள்ளன. 2026-ல் Nvidia போன்ற நிறுவனங்கள் சரிவைச் சந்தித்தாலும், Apple தனது மூலதனச் செலவுகளைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தியதும், Gemini உடனான ஒப்பந்தமும் அதன் வளர்ச்சிக்குக் காரணமாக அமைந்தன. சந்தையில் நிலவும் நிச்சயமற்ற சூழலில், முதலீட்டாளர்களுக்கு ஒரு பாதுகாப்பான முதலீட்டுத் தேர்வாக Apple உருவெடுத்துள்ளது.

title: Sand.ai’s MAGI-2 takes top image-to-video spot at a fraction of rivals’ price
summary:
Sand.ai's affordable MAGI-2 model could democratize high-quality image-to-video creation, challenging industry pricing norms and accessibility.
The post Sand.ai’s MAGI-2 takes top image-to-video spot at a fraction of rivals’ price appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Sand.ai has launched its new MAGI-2 model, which provides high-quality image-to-video generation capabilities. The model has reached a leading position in the industry while being offered at a significantly lower price point than competing services. By prioritizing affordability, Sand.ai aims to increase accessibility for creators and challenge existing market pricing standards for generative video technology.
content_ta: Sand.ai நிறுவனம் தனது புதிய MAGI-2 மாடலை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இது உயர்தர இமேஜ்-டு-வீடியோ உருவாக்கும் திறனை வழங்குகிறது. இந்த மாடல் சந்தையில் முன்னணியில் இருப்பதோடு, மற்ற நிறுவனங்களின் சேவைகளை விட மிகக் குறைந்த விலையில் கிடைக்கிறது. மலிவு விலையில் இந்தத் தொழில்நுட்பத்தை வழங்குவதன் மூலம், அதிகப்படியான படைப்பாளிகளுக்கு உதவும் வகையிலும், சந்தையில் நிலவும் விலை நிர்ணய முறையை மாற்றவும் Sand.ai முயற்சி செய்கிறது.

title: Anthropic and OpenAI proofs fuel speculation about AI’s threat to encryption
summary:
AI advancements in solving complex mathematical problems could undermine current encryption systems, posing significant security risks.
The post Anthropic and OpenAI proofs fuel speculation about AI’s threat to encryption appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Recent mathematical proofs demonstrated by Anthropic and OpenAI have sparked significant concern regarding the future of data security. Experts suggest that as these AI models become more adept at solving complex computational problems, they may eventually threaten the integrity of existing encryption standards. This development has triggered widespread industry speculation about potential risks to digital privacy and the urgent need to prepare for quantum-resistant cryptographic solutions.
content_ta: Anthropic மற்றும் OpenAI நிறுவனங்கள் முன்வைத்த புதிய கணித நிரூபணங்கள், தரவு பாதுகாப்பின் எதிர்காலம் குறித்த கவலைகளை ஏற்படுத்தியுள்ளன. சிக்கலான கணக்கீட்டு சிக்கல்களைத் தீர்க்கும் திறன் கொண்ட இந்த AI மாதிரிகள், காலப்போக்கில் தற்போதைய குறியாக்க முறைகளுக்கு (encryption standards) பெரும் அச்சுறுத்தலாக மாறக்கூடும் என்று நிபுணர்கள் எச்சரிக்கின்றனர். இந்த முன்னேற்றமானது, டிஜிட்டல் தனியுரிமைக்கு ஏற்படக்கூடிய அபாயங்கள் மற்றும் குவாண்டம்-எதிர்ப்பு பாதுகாப்பு தீர்வுகளை உருவாக்குவது குறித்த விவாதங்களை தொழில்நுட்பத் துறையில் வலுப்படுத்தியுள்ளது.

title: Fidelity Files for Chainlink ETF. What Does It Mean for LINK?
summary: Key takeaways Fidelity has filed to launch a Chainlink ETF (ticker FLNK) that would hold LINK directly and list on Nasdaq, but the filing is preliminary with no launch date or final fee. The fund would not stake its LINK, so shareholders would not receive staking rewards. Fidelity would enter a market that already has Grayscale (GLNK) and Bitwise (CLNK) LINK funds, and Charles Schwab offers direct LINK trading. A new listing does not automatically mean new LINK buying: only sustained net creations add to the fund’s holdings. Shares outstanding, LINK held and net creations after launch will show whether demand is genuinely new. Fidelity’s Chainlink ETF proposal would hold LINK directly and trade on Nasdaq if it clears the remaining steps. The proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, described in a November 25 registration statement, would use the ticker FLNK, although the filing is preliminary and no launch date or final annual fee has been provided. The larger question is not whether Wall Street can package LINK. It already has. The question is whether Fidelity can attract fresh demand for the token rather than divide the existing market among another set of fund shares. Fidelity’s Filing Is Specific About What Investors Would Own The proposed fund would hold LINK, not a basket of blockchain companies or derivatives intended to mimic LINK’s price. Its objective is to follow the token’s U.S. dollar performance, less expenses and liabilities. The prospectus identifies Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust and Coinbase Custody as custodians, with the trust intending to hold its LINK on Ethereum. Fidelity also lays out how the price would be measured. Its proposed reference rate uses prices from eligible LINK spot markets, with a volume-weighted median methodology calculated every 15 seconds using rolling 60-minute market data. That is a mechanism for valuing the assets. It is not a guarantee that fund shares will trade at precisely the reported value when markets are thin or volatile. Nor is this a yield product. The filing states plainly: “The Trust will not stake its LINK.” Shareholders would not receive staking rewards through the fund. They would be buying securities designed to reflect an underlying token’s price, not a wallet balance they can use in Chainlink services. That distinction matters because the company’s use of Chainlink technology elsewhere is a separate story. NewsBTC has previously reported on Chainlink infrastructure used with Fidelity’s tokenized FILQ fund. An investment vehicle that owns LINK is not evidence of increased demand for Chainlink’s oracle services, and using the network’s technology does not automatically mean buying its token. Fidelity Would Enter a Market That Already Has LINK Funds This is not the first attempt to make LINK available through conventional securities accounts. Grayscale’s Chainlink Trust ETF, trading as GLNK, had a share creation and redemption program in place from December 2025, according to its SEC disclosures. The Bitwise Chainlink ETF, CLNK, also appeared in a January 2026 Nasdaq information circular. And fund shares are not the only conventional route. In November, NewsBTC covered Charles Schwab’s rollout of direct LINK trading to eligible crypto clients. These routes do different things, but they establish a useful baseline: access is no longer the same problem it was when crypto products were confined to specialist exchanges. Fidelity’s possible advantage is distribution. Its name and brokerage relationships may reach customers who would not open a crypto wallet or buy LINK on a trading platform. That is a credible reason the filing matters. But branding, however recognizable, cannot tell investors how much money will arrive once trading begins. There is also the price of access. The preliminary prospectus leaves the sponsor’s annual fee blank. Until that figure is settled, it is impossible to make an honest cost comparison with competing LINK products. For investors choosing between wrappers around the same token, fees, trading spreads and the gap between share prices and net asset value deserve more attention than a new ticker. A New ETF Listing Would Not Automatically Mean New LINK Buying The mechanics are worth getting right. The proposed trust would issue and redeem large blocks of shares through authorized participants, using cash or LINK under procedures described in the filing. Everyday investors would generally trade the shares on an exchange instead of placing orders with the trust. Those are two different markets. When one investor sells an existing fund share to another, the trade does not by itself require the trust to acquire more LINK. Sustained net creations can increase a fund’s underlying holdings. Redemptions can do the reverse. A rising share price, meanwhile, may reflect a higher LINK price rather than additional tokens entering custody. That is why the announcement alone provides no evidence of fresh institutional inflows. The Form S-1 is a plan, not a subscription report. It does not tell us how much outside capital will be committed, what portion might come from rival products, or whether investor interest will survive a difficult crypto market. There is a fair counterargument. Fidelity could appeal to a materially different pool of investors and grow total demand rather than simply redistribute it. The filing establishes a possible channel for that to happen. It does not establish the outcome. What Would Actually Change the Assessment? First, the registration statement must become effective and the proposed Nasdaq listing must move forward. The final prospectus should also resolve the missing fee and other commercial details. Those are immediate milestones, not formalities to be assumed away. If the product launches, the more revealing evidence will arrive afterward: the number of LINK held, changes in shares outstanding, sustained net creations or redemptions, trading liquidity and discounts or premiums to net asset value. Comparisons with existing LINK funds would help separate fresh demand from investors moving between products. Until those figures exist, the sensible interpretation is narrow. Fidelity wants to sell investors exposure to Chainlink through a familiar brokerage format. Whether that changes the market for LINK is still an open question, and one that a filing cannot answer.
content: Fidelity Investments has filed for a new Chainlink ETF, dubbed FLNK, aiming to provide direct exposure to the token on Nasdaq. While the proposal highlights Fidelity’s distribution reach, it remains preliminary without a finalized fee or launch date. The fund will not offer staking rewards. Whether this product attracts significant new institutional demand or simply fragments existing market liquidity among current providers like Grayscale and Bitwise remains to be seen after its potential launch.
content_ta: Fidelity Investments நிறுவனம் Chainlink ETF-ஐ அறிமுகம் செய்ய விண்ணப்பித்துள்ளது. FLNK என அழைக்கப்படும் இந்த நிதி, Nasdaq தளத்தில் வர்த்தகம் செய்யப்படும். எனினும், இதற்கான கட்டணம் மற்றும் தொடக்கத் தேதி குறித்த விவரங்கள் இன்னும் இறுதி செய்யப்படவில்லை. இந்த நிதியில் ஸ்டேக்கிங் வெகுமதிகள் கிடைக்காது. Fidelity-ன் இந்த முயற்சி சந்தையில் புதிய முதலீடுகளை ஈர்க்குமா அல்லது Grayscale மற்றும் Bitwise போன்ற ஏற்கனவே உள்ள நிறுவனங்களுடனான போட்டியில் சந்தைப் பங்கை மட்டும் பிரிக்குமா என்பது, இந்த நிதி செயல்பாட்டுக்கு வந்த பிறகே தெரியவரும்.

content_ta: UK ரெங்குலேட்டர் DeFi விதிமுறைகளை கடுமையாக்க திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது. title: 1Password hacker stole customer names and emails, but vaults safe
summary: The password manager, which is used by millions of people to store their login credentials, said customer vaults were unaffected by the breach.
content: The password management service 1Password recently confirmed a security breach where hackers accessed customer contact information. The stolen data includes names and email addresses. However, the company assured users that their primary password vaults, which contain sensitive login credentials, remain secure and were not accessed during the incident. 1Password is currently investigating the breach to ensure ongoing protection for its millions of global users.
content_ta: கடவுச்சொல் மேலாண்மை சேவையான 1Password, தனது வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் பெயர் மற்றும் மின்னஞ்சல் முகவரிகள் திருடப்பட்டதாக உறுதிப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த பாதுகாப்பு மீறலில் வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் கடவுச்சொல் பெட்டகங்கள் (vaults) பாதிக்கப்படவில்லை என்றும், அவை பாதுகாப்பாக இருப்பதாகவும் நிறுவனம் தெரிவித்துள்ளது. லட்சக்கணக்கான பயனர்களைக் கொண்ட இந்த தளத்தில், ரகசியமான உள்நுழைவுத் தரவுகள் திருடப்படவில்லை என்பதை உறுதிப்படுத்திய 1Password, இந்த சம்பவம் குறித்து தொடர்ந்து விசாரணை நடத்தி வருகிறது.

title: LIVE – Crypto News Today: Is Bitcoin Bottoming Out? BTC Bounces Back After PCE Shock

content_ta: அண்மைய பணவீக்க தரவுகள் மற்றும் சந்தை ஏற்ற இறக்கங்களைத் தொடர்ந்து, Bitcoin தனது விலையை மீண்டும் $60,000 நோக்கி உயர்த்தியுள்ளது. title: Switzerland’s Crypto Tax Data Deal Could Make Bitcoin Holdings Less Private
summary: Key takeaways Switzerland’s Federal Council approved 57 potential partner jurisdictions for automatic exchange of crypto tax data, starting in 2028. The system follows the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF); exchanges must identify customers’ tax residency and report activity. It creates no new crypto tax. It changes how governments obtain information to enforce existing obligations. Moving […]
content: Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 partner jurisdictions to begin the automatic exchange of crypto tax data by 2028. Following the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), the mandate requires exchanges to identify customer tax residency and report activity. While this does not introduce new taxes, it significantly improves government access to information for enforcing existing tax obligations, potentially impacting the privacy traditionally associated with holding Bitcoin and other digital assets.
content_ta: Switzerland-ன் Federal Council, 2028 முதல் 57 நாடுகள் மற்றும் பிராந்தியங்களுடன் தானியங்கி முறையில் கிரிப்டோ வரி தரவுகளைப் பகிர்ந்துகொள்ள ஒப்புதல் அளித்துள்ளது. OECD-ன் Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) வழிகாட்டுதலின்படி, இனி கிரிப்டோ பரிமாற்றங்கள் வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் வரி குடியிருப்பு விவரங்களைச் சேகரித்து சமர்ப்பிக்க வேண்டும். புதிய வரி விதிப்புகள் இல்லையென்றாலும், அரசாங்கங்கள் வரி ஏய்ப்பைக் கண்காணிக்க இந்த நடவடிக்கை உதவும். இது Bitcoin போன்ற சொத்துக்களின் தனிநபர் ரகசியத்தன்மையில் மாற்றங்களை ஏற்படுத்தக்கூடும்.

title: Bitcoin’s Recovery Faces a New Warning After $2 Billion in ETF Outflows
summary: Key takeaways US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $2.05 billion in combined net outflows over four straight sessions ending November 24, per Farside Investors, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for roughly $1.77 billion. Bitcoin is back above $60,000 after trading as low as about $55,300 on November 21, according to Glassnode. Reclaiming $60,000 does not by itself confirm the correction is over: holders who bought near that level may sell into the rebound. Bitcoin trades far beyond US ETFs, so outflows are not proof of further downside, but a recovery that holds despite redemptions would be a stronger signal. Thanksgiving closes US markets, so the missing ETF data is not a sign of improved demand. Friday’s session will be more telling. The Bitcoin recovery above $60,000 is offering some relief after a brutal November sell-off, but the money flowing through US spot Bitcoin ETFs tells a less encouraging story. The funds recorded more than $2 billion in combined net outflows over four consecutive trading sessions ending November 24. Bitcoin’s return to the psychologically important price level follows a difficult week in which the cryptocurrency traded as low as approximately $55,300. The rebound is welcome. What is less clear is whether buyers have returned with enough capital to sustain it. Bitcoin ETFs Are Still Losing Money The scale of the recent withdrawals deserves more attention than the recovery itself. According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $582.3 million on November 19, followed by another $669.2 million the next day. Withdrawals continued on Monday and Tuesday, bringing the combined total across those four trading sessions to approximately $2.05 billion. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for roughly $1.77 billion in net outflows during that period. Wednesday’s figures are still subject to final reporting confirmation, although available data points to further withdrawals. These numbers do not mean that every institutional investor is abandoning Bitcoin. ETF shareholders include different types of investors, from financial advisers and asset managers to individual traders. Some may be reducing risk, while others could be unwinding positions that were never intended as long-term investments. What the figures establish is that the ETF market has experienced persistent net redemptions, even after Bitcoin’s substantial decline. That is not the response bulls would ideally want to see from buyers following a major correction. Bitcoin’s Drop Below $60,000 Exposed a Deeper Problem Earlier this week, Bitcoin fell below $60,000 again after an initial recovery above $64,000 failed to hold. Glassnode’s November 24 report, titled The Canary in the Coal Mine, documented the severity of Bitcoin’s latest decline. The cryptocurrency reached approximately $55,300 on November 21, falling beneath the lows established during the summer. That matters because investors who bought during previous corrections may now be sitting on losses despite having entered the market at what appeared to be relatively attractive prices. Glassnode’s historical data reveals another uncomfortable detail. Long-term holders recently accounted for more than 75% of Bitcoin’s realized losses before their share fell back toward 50%. Similar periods of selling at a loss appeared during previous bear markets, although that alone does not establish that Bitcoin has reached a bottom. Their behavior becomes particularly important when Bitcoin starts recovering. Some holders may use a rebound to reduce their exposure or exit positions closer to their original purchase price. Others may be willing to hold through further volatility. Which group dominates will influence how much buying is required to sustain the next move higher. A price that previously attracted buyers can become an area of selling pressure when the market approaches it from below. This is one reason why reclaiming $60,000 should not automatically be interpreted as confirmation that the correction has ended. A Market Bottom Does Not Require Everyone to Turn Bullish There is a credible argument against interpreting persistent ETF outflows as evidence that Bitcoin must fall further. Markets can begin recovering before investor sentiment improves. In fact, waiting for every major indicator to turn positive can mean missing a substantial portion of a reversal. Glassnode’s latest research offers some historical perspective. Bitcoin’s realized losses relative to capital inflows over the preceding year have reached their highest intensity since the FTX collapse in 2022. Previous episodes of heavy losses have occurred near major market bottoms, but severe selling alone is not enough to confirm that a recovery is underway. Bitcoin also trades across a much broader market than US exchange-traded funds. Direct purchases, overseas exchanges and other investment vehicles can absorb selling even when American funds experience redemptions. The distinction is between evidence that a market can recover and evidence that it has already established a sustainable recovery. Bitcoin’s latest bounce demonstrates that buyers are willing to step in at lower prices. It does not yet establish whether those buyers can absorb additional selling at higher levels. If Bitcoin begins to hold its gains despite persistent ETF withdrawals, that would itself be an encouraging development. It would suggest that demand elsewhere in the market is capable of offsetting some of the pressure coming from the funds. For now, the price and ETF data leave that question open. Thanksgiving Could Make Bitcoin’s Next Move Harder to Read Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday adds another complication to the recovery. US equity markets are closed, removing a regular trading session for American spot Bitcoin ETFs while cryptocurrency exchanges continue operating. The absence of new ETF flow figures during the holiday should not be confused with an improvement in institutional demand. With fewer traditional financial market participants active, Bitcoin’s immediate price movements may also provide an incomplete picture of how investors are responding to the recent sell-off. Friday’s shortened US trading session and the subsequent return to normal market hours will provide more useful evidence. For traders, the important signals are whether Bitcoin can retain its recent gains, whether ETF redemptions begin to ease and whether buying remains strong enough to absorb selling when normal market participation resumes. The $60,000 level may dominate the headlines, but the more convincing recovery will be the one that can survive without depending entirely on temporary relief from selling pressure.
content: Bitcoin has climbed back above $60,000 following a severe November sell-off that saw prices drop near $55,300. However, US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded over $2 billion in net outflows across four consecutive sessions, raising questions about whether the recovery can be sustained. While the rebound offers brief relief, analysts note that continuing redemptions and potential selling pressure near the $60,000 level mean the correction may not be over yet.

content: Hong Kong-based crypto trading firm Auros is reportedly winding down its operations. title: Bitcoin little changed, DeFi tokens lead the bounce as U.S. marks Thanksgiving

DeFi மற்றும் இன்ஃப்ராஸ்ட்ரக்சர் டோக்கன்கள் சந்தையின் மீட்சியை முன்னின்று நடத்தி, முன்னணி கிரிப்டோகரன்சியை விட கிட்டத்தட்ட இருமடங்கு லாபத்தைப் பெற்றன.

title: Nvidia shipment freeze and U.S. chip curbs put AI stocks under pressure
summary: U.S. export controls have halted Nvidia server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries and put billions in data centre financing under review.
content: Recent U.S. export controls have frozen Nvidia server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries. These strict regulations have placed significant pressure on AI-related stocks as billions of dollars in planned data centre financing face uncertain reviews and potential delays.

title: New York Attorney General wins $1.4 billion ruling against founders of crypto trading firm NovaTech
summary: AWS Mining and NovaTech founders Cynthia and Eddie Petion were ordered to pay $1.37 billion after defrauding hundreds of thousands of people, including 11,000 New Yorkers.
content: The New York Attorney General has won a massive $1.4 billion ruling against the founders of crypto trading firm NovaTech. Founders Cynthia and Eddie Petion, along with AWS Mining, were ordered to pay $1.37 billion for defrauding hundreds of thousands of investors, including thousands of residents in New York, through a large-scale fraudulent scheme.
content_ta: Crypto trading firm NovaTech நிறுவனத்தின் நிறுவனர்களுக்கு எதிராக New York Attorney General $1.4 பில்லியன் தொகையை வென்றுள்ளார். ஆயிரக்கணக்கான முதலீட்டாளர்களை ஏமாற்றியதற்காக Founders Cynthia மற்றும் Eddie Petion மற்றும் AWS Mining ஆகியோருக்கு $1.37 பில்லியன் செலுத்த உத்தரவிடப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Switzerland approves 57 jurisdictions for crypto data exchange from 2028
summary: The Swiss Federal Council cleared 57 potential partners for cryptoasset tax-information exchanges beginning in 2028.
content: The Swiss Federal Council has approved 57 jurisdictions for the automatic exchange of cryptoasset tax information. Beginning in 2028, Switzerland will partner with these regions to share financial data regarding cryptoassets. This move aligns with international efforts to enhance tax transparency and prevent tax evasion involving digital assets.
content_ta: சுவிட்சர்லாந்து பெடரல் கவுன்சில், cryptoasset வரி தகவல் பரிமாற்றத்திற்காக 57 அதிகார வரம்புகளுக்கு ஒப்புதல் அளித்துள்ளது. 2028 ஆம் ஆண்டு முதல், cryptoassets தொடர்பான நிதித் தரவைப் பகிர சுவிட்சர்லாந்து இந்தப் பகுதிகளுடன் கூட்டாளеாகச் செயல்படும். வரி வெளிப்படைத்தன்மையை மேம்படுத்துவதற்கும் டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்கள் சம்பந்தப்பட்ட வரி ஏய்ப்பு தடுப்பு நடவடிக்கைகளுக்கும் சர்வதேச முயற்சிகளுக்கு இந்த நடவடிக்கை ஒத்துப்போகிறது.

title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Faces a 9% Jump at the Worst Possible Time for Miners
summary: Key takeaways Bitcoin mining difficulty is on course to rise about 9% on November 27, from 134.82 trillion toward 147 trillion, reversing much of the 9.13% cut on November 14. Under otherwise unchanged conditions, a 9% increase cuts expected BTC output per unit of hashrate by roughly 8.3%. At about $28 per petahash per day, a fleet running at 20 J/TH and $0.05/kWh would see its electricity-adjusted margin fall from about $4 to under $2. The effect is uneven: efficient operators with cheap power can absorb it, while older fleets may switch machines off. Difficulty alone is not evidence of more miner selling; miner balances, exchange transfers and treasury disclosures are. Bitcoin mining difficulty is on course to increase by approximately 9% at the next network adjustment, expected on November 27. The increase would reverse much of the relief miners received less than two weeks ago, leaving operators facing tougher competition for block rewards while Bitcoin trades well below its previous highs. Current network estimates put mining difficulty at 134.82 trillion, following a 9.13% reduction on November 14. If the projected increase holds, difficulty will climb back toward 147 trillion. For miners struggling to keep their machines profitable, the timing is hardly ideal. The electricity bill remains largely unchanged, but the same hardware could soon generate less Bitcoin. Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Is Reversing November’s Relief Bitcoin adjusts its mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to maintain an average block production time of approximately ten minutes. When blocks are produced too quickly, the network makes the mathematical conditions for discovering new blocks more demanding. When production slows, difficulty moves in the opposite direction. The previous 9.13% reduction in Bitcoin mining difficulty gave active miners some breathing room. Operators could expect to earn more Bitcoin from the same amount of computing power, provided other conditions remained comparable. That advantage now appears temporary. The upcoming adjustment, expected at block 977,760, reflects a faster pace of block production during the current difficulty period. A 9% increase in difficulty does not translate into an identical percentage reduction in mining revenue. Under otherwise unchanged conditions, expected Bitcoin production per unit of computing power would decline by approximately 8.3%. Consider an operator whose machines currently generate 1 BTC over a given period. Following a 9% difficulty increase, the same machines would be expected to produce approximately 0.917 BTC over an equivalent period. Nothing about the hardware needs to change for that reduction to occur. The network has simply raised the amount of work required to compete for its rewards. The Real Problem Is What Miners Earn From Their Machines Mining difficulty only tells part of the story. A more useful measure of the industry’s financial condition is hashprice, which tracks the expected revenue generated by a given amount of computing power over a day. Hashprice incorporates Bitcoin’s market value, network difficulty and transaction fee revenue. It provides a clearer indication of whether a miner’s hardware is generating enough income to justify keeping it switched on. Recent network data from mining industry trackers puts daily hashprice at around $28 per petahash of computing power. At that level, the economics can become uncomfortable surprisingly quickly. Consider a hypothetical mining fleet with an energy efficiency of 20 joules per terahash and an electricity rate of $0.05 per kilowatt-hour. Operating one petahash of computing power continuously would cost approximately $24 per day in electricity alone. Against $28 in gross daily mining revenue, that leaves just $4 before hosting, maintenance, cooling, financing and other expenses. If difficulty rises by 9% while Bitcoin’s price and average fees per block remain unchanged, that daily revenue would fall to approximately $25.69. The remaining electricity-adjusted margin would shrink to less than $2. The network adjustment is the same for everyone. Its financial consequences are not. An operator with newer machines and inexpensive power may comfortably absorb the change. Another running older equipment could find that switching off part of its fleet makes more financial sense than continuing to mine. Bitcoin Miners Are Already Rethinking Their Business Models The industry’s response to difficult mining economics extends beyond upgrading machines or negotiating cheaper electricity. Some established Bitcoin mining businesses are redirecting infrastructure toward artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. Access to substantial electricity capacity, established data centers and existing infrastructure gives certain operators alternatives that smaller mining businesses may not have. This does not mean Bitcoin mining is disappearing. The projected difficulty increase itself suggests that blocks are being produced faster than the protocol’s target rate during the current adjustment period. But the growing divergence between mining operators deserves attention. A Bitcoin mining facility with access to inexpensive energy and efficient equipment operates under a very different set of economic conditions from a business relying on expensive financing and aging machines. Rising difficulty does not necessarily make the entire industry unprofitable. It makes the difference between efficient and inefficient operators harder to ignore. Does Higher Mining Difficulty Mean More Bitcoin Selling? The prospect of shrinking margins raises an obvious question for Bitcoin investors: will miners need to sell more BTC to finance their operations? There is a plausible case for additional selling from businesses facing substantial operating expenses or debt repayments. Mining companies cannot generally settle their electricity bills with anticipated future Bitcoin rewards. However, network difficulty alone provides no evidence that miners have increased their Bitcoin sales. Some operators hold substantial treasury reserves. Others sell their production regularly, regardless of market conditions. Businesses can also reduce operating expenses, shut down inefficient equipment or obtain financing instead of liquidating additional holdings. Actual miner balance data, exchange transfers and company treasury disclosures will provide more useful evidence than the difficulty adjustment itself. The immediate development to watch is whether the estimated increase materializes at the next adjustment block. After that, hashprice and changes in network computing power will help reveal how operators are responding. Bitcoin’s protocol is doing exactly what it was designed to do. It adjusts the competition for block rewards without considering whether individual mining businesses can afford to remain competitive. The machines that become uneconomical have always been the operators’ problem, not the network’s.
content: Bitcoin mining difficulty is projected to jump by approximately 9% on November 27, reversing much of the relief seen from a recent reduction. This increase will raise competition for block rewards and squeeze electricity-adjusted profit margins for miners, particularly those operating older equipment. While efficient operators can absorb the change, others may be forced to shut down machines or pivot toward artificial intelligence infrastructure.

title: Paybacks Raises $10M Pre-Series A From Foresight Ventures
summary:
Paybacks today announced a $10 million Pre-Series A investment from Foresight Ventures and the official launch of paybacks.io, a platform that returns a portion of crypto futures trading fees to traders as cashback.
Foresight Ventures is the sole investor in the round, acquiring a 10% stake at a $100 million valuation. The funding announcement and platform launch come as Paybacks begins offering its cashback service through agreements with participating crypto exchanges.
Under a typical exchange referral arrangement, the exchange pays a commission based on trading fees generated by users who joined through a partner’s link. Paybacks uses the commissions it receives under its exchange agreements to provide cashback to the traders whose activity generated them. Depending on the applicable rate, eligible traders can receive up to 90% of their futures trading fees back.
Cashback is credited automatically in USDT to a trader’s exchange account the day after an eligible trade. For a trader who pays $1,000 in eligible fees, the maximum rate would mean $900 in cashback. The amount received depends on the rate applicable to that trader’s exchange account.
Paybacks is also launching with its Highest Cashback Guarantee. If a trader finds a higher cashback rate elsewhere, Paybacks says it will match that rate under the guarantee.
To use the platform, a trader signs up for a participating exchange through Paybacks and links their exchange UID. Once the account is linked, eligible trading activity generates cashback for payment the following day. Paybacks offers 24-hour live support, including assistance for traders seeking to move an existing exchange account, and plans to add more exchanges after launch.

title: OpenWay Joins Visa Digitalization Ready Program to Accelerate Digital Payment Adoption in Asia Pacific
summary:
OpenWay, a global provider of digital payment software and developer of the Way4 platform, has joined the Visa Digitalization Ready Program (VDRP) in Asia Pacific. The collaboration with Visa, a world leader in digital payments, supports financial institutions in implementing eligible Visa digital payment solutions, with an initial focus on Visa Flexible Credential and Click to Pay.
Through the program, OpenWay and Visa aim to accelerate client implementations, expand adoption of Visa payment capabilities and create additional business opportunities for their mutual clients across the region. Participation strengthens OpenWay’s ability to help banks, processors and fintechs bring new payment services to market on Way4, translating payment innovation into practical benefits for consumers and businesses.
Financial institutions face a dual challenge: responding to demand for more convenient digital payments while managing the cost and complexity of introducing new services. Customers increasingly expect greater control over how they pay and straightforward online checkout. Meeting these expectations requires coordination between payment networks, technology providers and the institutions delivering the customer experience.
VDRP supports the implementation of eligible Visa digital payment solutions in Asia Pacific. OpenWay’s participation brings this support together with Way4’s capabilities in card issuing, transaction processing and digital payments, helping clients move from product planning to implementation more efficiently.
“Visa is focused on making e-commerce seamless and secure for customers, merchants and financial institutions,” said Krishna Thiruvengadam, Head of Core Platform & Digital Solutions. “OpenWay’s participation in the Visa Digitalization Ready Program brings together Visa’s digital payment capabilities and Way4’s processing platform to help accelerate deployment of these digital innovations across Asia Pacific. Starting with Visa Flexible Credential and Click to Pay, we see a strong opportunity to help our mutual clients create differentiated payment experiences and unlock new opportunities for growth.”
“Financial institutions want to turn payment innovation into services that customers choose to use every day,” said Rudy Gunawan, Managing Director of OpenWay Asia. “Joining the Visa Digitalization Ready Program strengthens our collaboration with Visa in Asia Pacific and helps our clients bring these services to market more efficiently. Our initial focus brings together two clear customer benefits: greater flexibility in how people fund their purchases and less effort when they pay online.”
Greater payment choice through one credential
Visa Flexible Credential enables a single payment credential to provide access to multiple funding sources. Depending on the issuer’s offering, customers can use it to access options such as debit or credit, with choices managed through their financial institution.
For cardholders, this creates a more convenient way to use different payment options through a familiar credential. It gives issuers opportunities to design innovative propositions around customers’ financial needs, connect distinct existing products and offer additional services within their banking relationship.
Way4 supports the processing and configuration capabilities financial institutions need to develop these propositions. OpenWay’s participation in VDRP supports client implementation of Visa Flexible Credential, helping issuers translate payment flexibility into differentiated products for their markets.
Easier online payments with Click to Pay
Click to Pay simplifies online checkout by enabling consumers to pay with enrolled cards without having to repeatedly enter their card details at participating merchants. It addresses a familiar source of friction in digital commerce: the effort required to find a card and complete payment forms.
For issuers, Click to Pay can support customer engagement and card usage by making their cards easier to use online. For merchants, a simpler checkout experience can help reduce cart abandonment and make it easier for customers to complete their purchases. Consumers benefit from a more consistent way to pay across participating online stores, with security built into the payment experience.
Way4 already supports Visa Click to Pay. OpenWay’s participation in VDRP builds on this foundation to support client implementations and wider adoption across Asia Pacific, helping more financial institutions offer Click to Pay to their cardholders and incorporate it into their digital payment offerings.
Supporting continued innovation on Way4
Joining VDRP advances OpenWay’s strategy of helping clients develop and scale payment services on a flexible platform. Way4 combines card issuing, merchant acquiring, digital wallets and transaction switching on a single real-time platform, giving financial institutions a foundation for expanding their payment businesses.
For processors serving multiple financial institutions, the ability to introduce new capabilities through a common platform is particularly valuable. For banks and fintechs, it supports a continuing product roadmap as customer needs and market opportunities evolve.
The initial scope of OpenWay’s VDRP participation covers Visa Flexible Credential and Click to Pay, with the potential to include additional eligible Visa solutions over time. The collaboration is focused on Asia Pacific and supports a shared objective: making it easier for financial institutions to implement payment capabilities that deliver meaningful customer value.

title: Government Reappoints AI Champions to Drive the Next Phase of AI in Financial Services
summary:
Technology experts Harriet Rees and Dr. Rohit Dhawan have been reappointed as the government’s Financial Services AI Champions until 2027, helping support the UK remain a global leader in the safe and innovative use of AI in financial services.
The two Champions will coordinate delivery of industry recommendations in the Financial Services AI Adoption Plan, helping accelerate safe and responsible adoption of AI and unlocking greater productivity and competitiveness across the sector.
The Economic Secretary Lucy Rigby will announce the reappointments of Ms Rees and Dr. Dhawan, of Starling Bank and Lloyds Bank respectively, today (25 November 2026) during a keynote speech at the techUK summit on AI sovereignty in financial services. Her speech will emphasise the importance of safe adoption of AI at scale and at pace, encouraging firms to test, deploy and scale AI while ensuring accountability remains clear.
AI is already transforming financial services, delivering better outcomes for consumers and supporting growth across the UK economy. The financial sector has been one of the fastest adopters of AI, with 86% of UK financial firms now having deployed AI systems.
Economic Secretary to the Treasury, Lucy Rigby KC MP, said:
From driving productivity and growth to helping to deliver better services, the safe adoption of AI is key to the future of financial services.
Harriet and Rohit have already proven their dedication to ensuring the UK remains a world leader in AI adoption across financial services, and I’m delighted both have accepted extensions to their terms of appointment.
AI is helping firms tackle fraud and financial crime, strengthen risk management and improve services for consumers, while creating significant opportunities to grow enterprise productivity. As the technology develops, the government is focused on ensuring firms of all sizes have the confidence, clarity and support needed to adopt AI safely and at scale, while maintaining high levels of public trust.
Since their appointment in January, the two Champions have brought together industry, regulators and other stakeholders to identify opportunities to build on the responsible use of AI. Their Financial Services AI Adoption Plan, published in July, set out practical recommendations to overcome barriers to adoption and ensure the UK remains an attractive place to develop, deploy and scale AI-enabled financial services.
The Champions will continue to draw on their deep industry networks and extensive expertise in this field to support and coordinate delivery of the Plan’s recommendations. They will continue to engage with firms and regulators to ensure voices across the sector are reflected in the UK’s approach to AI in financial services.
Harriet Rees, Group Chief Information Officer – Starling Bank, said: 
Being reappointed as AI Champion for Financial Services comes at a pivotal moment as the sector moves from ambition to delivery. Alongside HM Treasury, the regulators, and wider industry, I am focused on driving practical progress - unlocking the potential of agentic AI and modernised advice, while managing concentration risk and clarifying the regulatory perimeter. The UK financial services sector is leading the way in AI adoption, and we have a real opportunity to turn that early lead into lasting economic advantage. Accelerating responsible adoption can boost productivity and growth, deliver better outcomes for consumers and businesses, and reinforce the UK’s position as a world-leading financial centre.
I’m looking forward to continuing as AI Champion and turning our recommendations into action. That means ensuring regulation, including the regulatory perimeter, keeps pace with AI. Strengthening resilience, building the skills our industry needs and unlocking the next wave of innovation in agentic payments will also be critical. Collaboration between industry, regulators and government will be essential to removing barriers, building trust and maximising the economic opportunity AI presents for the UK.
At Budget 2026, Chancellor John Healey set out Britain’s distinctive approach to AI; managing risks responsibly, ambitious about the opportunity, and backed by the institutions, capabilities and infrastructure needed to manage the transition.

title: Most Europeans Take Payment Security on Faith
summary:
Almost three quarters of Europeans (74%) trust their bank to keep their payments secure, but just 22% feel they understand how those payments are protected, according to new research from Enfuce, Europe's card issuing and processing powerhouse. The findings come from a survey of 4,000 adults in France, Germany, Italy and the Netherlands. That sense of safety offers little protection when a scam arrives.
Key findings
13% of consumers who feel they understand payment security well said they shared personal or payment details after a phishing email without losing money in the past two years, compared with 4% of those who feel they do not understand it well.
74% trust banks to keep their payments secure, but just 22% feel they understand well how that protection works.
41% would feel uncomfortable if AI handled fraud detection on their payments instead of a human team. Only 20% would feel comfortable.
Just 19% would trust AI to make or manage payments, the lowest level of trust among the ten everyday tasks surveyed.
Consumers trust banks but are less sure how their payments are protected
Almost three quarters of consumers (74%) trust banks to keep their payments secure, yet just 22% feel they understand well how those payments are protected. The findings suggest that people put their faith in the bank, even when they are less sure how it protects them. Fintech and payment apps do not inspire the same confidence: just 27% trust them to keep their payments secure.
Dutch consumers are the most trusting of banks, while Italians are least likely to feel they understand payment security well. Banks are trusted by 83% of consumers in the Netherlands, 71% in Germany and France, and 70% in Italy. Far fewer feel they understand payment security well: 27% in the Netherlands, 26% in Germany, 18% in France and 17% in Italy.
Consumers disagree on who should pay after a scam
More than half (53%) would contact their bank first after suspected payment fraud. But asking for help does not mean holding the bank responsible: only 13% think it should be mainly responsible for the loss when someone is tricked into paying a fraudster.
French consumers are more than twice as likely as German consumers to contact their bank first after suspected fraud (77% versus 38%), even though trust in banks is 71% in both countries.
The Dutch are the most likely to say the person who was tricked should be mainly responsible for the loss: 42% take that view, compared with 10% in Germany and 16% in France and Italy. Those who feel they understand payment security well are also more likely to hold this view (26%, compared with 18% among the less confident).
Few people would trust AI with their payments
Almost everyone (94%) would accept at least one extra safeguard for more secure payments, but only 13% would accept AI being used to detect fraud. Of the ten tasks tested, making or managing payments is where people trust AI least (19%).
Of the ten everyday tasks surveyed, making or managing payments is where consumers trust AI least. Just 19% would trust AI to help with payments, compared with 56% who would trust it as a search engine and 22% who would trust it for mental health or emotional support.
The main worry is that AI could make mistakes (46%). Asked what would most increase their trust in any payment method, consumers most often chose knowing they would get their money back if something went wrong (25%). The research suggests payment providers need to be clearer about what help people can expect if protection fails, and that protection.
“People should not need to be payment security experts to keep their money safe. Our research shows why protection cannot depend on how confident someone feels. It has to be built into the systems they use. AI can help strengthen that protection, but the industry has to earn people’s trust in it. Consumers need to know how their money is protected and who will put things right if something goes wrong. That responsibility stays with us as the technology changes.” Denise Johansson, CEO and Co-founder of Enfuce said.

title: Stablecoin Fees Could Add 10% to a $20 Purchase, Research Finds Ahead of Black Friday
summary:
Customers paying merchants directly from cryptocurrency exchanges could face significant additional costs when using stablecoins, according to new research from Orbital, ahead of Black Friday.
Around 70% of stablecoin checkout payments to Orbital’s merchants came directly from cryptocurrency exchanges rather than personal wallets, according to Orbital’s payment processing data for August to October 2026. Customers paying this way may face an exchange withdrawal fee when sending their payment, adding to the purchase price even though the charge sits outside the merchant’s checkout.
Orbital analysed 24.8 million withdrawals of USDT and USDC, the two most popular stablecoins, worth $184.7 billion from 11 major exchanges in October 2026 for its report, The Real Cost of Stablecoin Checkout, estimating total withdrawal fees of $17.3 million.
It found that high withdrawal fees could add a staggering 10% to a $20 purchase.
Key findings include:
Small checkout payments can carry disproportionately high fees
More than half (51%) of the exchange withdrawals analysed were worth less than $100, while over a third were below $50. 
Because exchanges often charge flat withdrawal fees, smaller transactions can be disproportionately expensive. At 3 November fees, the median Tron withdrawal fee of $1.50 adds 7.5% to a hypothetical $20 payment. At Binance’s $2 Tron withdrawal fee, recorded on 16 November, this rises to 10%. 
On the other hand, the median USDT withdrawal fee on BNB Chain was just one cent, based on exchange fees recorded on 3 November – equivalent to 0.05% of a $20 payment. For merchants accepting smaller purchases, offering lower-cost compatible networks could make stablecoin checkout payments more affordable.
The networks merchants accept can significantly affect payment costs
Tron handled 39% of the withdrawals analysed but generated 83% of estimated fees, worth approximately $14.4 million. BNB Chain processed a similar share of withdrawals, at 37%, but accounted for just 2.6% of fees. 
Withdrawal fees can change overnight 
On 1 November, Binance raised its Tron withdrawal fee from $1.50 to $4, before reducing it again to $2 by 16 November. 
Across 201 withdrawal routes compared between January and 3 November, 53 became more expensive and 59 became cheaper. On 3 November, 17% of listed withdrawal routes were paused, making them unavailable for transfers at that time. 
Costs also vary sharply between exchanges. In October, Crypto.com’s average withdrawal fee was $4.62 – more than eight times higher than Binance’s.
Choosing cheaper networks could cut withdrawal fees by 98%
Orbital estimates that total fees across the withdrawals analysed could have fallen from $17.3 million to approximately $340,000 if every withdrawal had used the cheapest available network for the same stablecoin on its exchange.
That represents a theoretical reduction of 98%, illustrating how much network choice can affect costs. 
Why this matters for merchants
As stablecoins become a more practical way to pay, businesses need to think about the costs customers face when using them. Orbital’s payment data shows that direct exchange-to-merchant transfers are already a meaningful use case, making withdrawal fees relevant to the overall cost of paying with stablecoins. 
The wider research covers exchange withdrawals generally, rather than merchant purchases alone. However, it highlights potential challenges as businesses explore stablecoins for consumer transactions. 
“While it’s too early to say how quickly direct exchange-to-merchant payments will grow, merchants need to be prepared as stablecoin payments become more popular,” said Luke Wingfield Digby, co-founder and Head of Corporate Development of Orbital. 
“Merchants can’t control exchange withdrawal fees, but they can offer customers a choice of compatible and lower-cost networks. Getting that right now could help make stablecoin checkout payments more affordable and easier to use as adoption grows, while reducing friction and potentially improving conversion.”
* The analysis covers exchange withdrawals generally, rather than merchant purchases alone.

title: Unzer Expands Ecosystem With Tap to Pay: Smartphones Become Payment Terminals and Cash Registers
summary:
Unzer, one of Europe’s leading payment and software solution providers, has launched Tap to Pay, a new solution aimed at small and medium-sized businesses. With Tap to Pay, any NFC-enabled Android smartphone can be turned into a fully functional payment terminal without the need for any additional hardware. Merchants simply need the Unzer app to accept contactless card payments or payments made by smartphone or smartwatch directly. The underlying technology is known as SoftPOS (Software Point of Sale).
 
With Tap to Pay, Unzer is responding to the growing demand for flexible and mobile payment solutions. The offering is particularly well-suited to hospitality businesses, food trucks, market stalls, service providers and small retailers who want to accept payments wherever their customers are.
 
What makes Unzer's solution unique is that Tap to Pay is available not only as a standalone payment solution, but also in combination with Unzer's POS software. This turns an Android smartphone into both a payment terminal and a mobile cash register. Merchants can record sales and accept payments on the same device, without the need for additional POS hardware or payment terminals. In restaurants, staff can also use a single smartphone to take orders directly at the table and then accept payments.
 

“Today, commerce happens everywhere: in-store, online and on the go. With Tap to Pay, we make the entry into digital payments easier than ever before: in just a few minutes, an Android smartphone can become not only a secure payment terminal but also a fully functional mobile POS system,” says Isabelle Bénard, Chief Product and AI Officer at Unzer.
 
The launch of Tap to Pay is another step in expanding Unzer’s ecosystem, which brings together payments, software, and financial services on a single platform. Recently, Unzer extended its offering to include Unzer Financial Services. The solution features a business account and a corporate credit card with no monthly account fees. Incoming payments are instantly available in the merchant’s business account, while all financial and payment data is consolidated within the UnzerOne dashboard.
 

“Every merchant should have access to the same digital tools to manage their business easily - regardless of their size. With Tap to Pay, we are adding a particularly simple and flexible way to accept payments anywhere,” says Bénard.
 
The new solution is available to merchants in Germany with immediate effect.

title: Zcash Whale Wakes Up After 9 Years, Moves $11.39 Million To Kraken
summary: Key takeaways Lookonchain reports a Zcash whale moved 15,750 ZEC, about $11.39 million, to Kraken after nine years. The whale reportedly bought 23,412 ZEC in 2017 at about $215 (just over $5 million). The deposit is roughly two-thirds of that position. At about $723 per ZEC, the coins are worth around $8 million more than their estimated cost, a gain of roughly 236%. A deposit to an exchange is not proof of a sale, and the acquisition price is an estimate, not a verified record. More early holders moving dormant coins to exchanges could mean new Zcash buyers absorb supply from older holders. Nine years is an eternity in crypto. Yet one Zcash whale appears to have spent that long sitting on an investment made during the privacy coin’s early days. On Thursday, blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain reported that the investor had moved 15,750 ZEC, worth $11.39 million, to Kraken. The coins date back to 2017, when Ethereum was still a relatively young network, decentralized finance barely existed and Zcash was attempting to establish itself as a more private alternative to Bitcoin. Almost a decade later, the wallet is active again. And its owner’s reported acquisition price makes the transaction particularly interesting. A $5 Million Bet On Zcash In 2017 According to Lookonchain, the whale originally acquired 23,412 ZEC at an average price of approximately $215, representing an investment of just over $5 million. The latest transactions account for roughly two-thirds of that original position, with at least 7,750 ZEC transferred to a Kraken deposit address. At the reported transfer valuation of approximately $723 per ZEC, those 15,750 coins are worth around $8 million more than their estimated acquisition cost. That would represent a return of approximately 236% if the investor sold them at that price. What makes this wallet fascinating, however, is what happened between those two valuations. Zcash spent much of 2024 and early 2025 trading around $16 to $20 before staging a remarkable comeback. At $20 per coin, the whale’s original investment would have been worth less than $470,000, a paper loss of more than 90%, assuming the position remained intact. Holding an asset through a temporary market correction is one thing. Holding it through years of declining relevance, while newer cryptocurrencies attract developers, investors and attention, is something else entirely. Whatever the owner’s reasons for keeping the coins untouched, the decision has aged considerably better than it appeared to during Zcash’s quieter years. The Interesting Paradox Behind A Zcash Whale There is something almost ironic about the fact that investors are following the movements of a whale holding one of crypto’s best-known privacy coins. Unlike networks where transaction privacy is mandatory, Zcash supports both transparent and shielded transactions. Transparent addresses allow observers to examine balances and transfers, while shielded transactions use zero-knowledge cryptography to conceal transaction details. That distinction explains how blockchain monitoring platforms can identify certain large ZEC movements despite the cryptocurrency’s privacy capabilities. It also explains why the available information tells only part of the story. Lookonchain can identify an apparent exchange deposit and estimate its value. Establishing who controls the wallet, whether ownership changed privately during those nine years or what the investor intends to do next is considerably harder. Even the reported acquisition price is an estimate rather than a verified record of the owner’s personal trading history. That is an important limitation of on-chain analysis, particularly when dealing with a network explicitly designed to give users greater control over their financial visibility. Zcash’s Comeback Has Given Early Investors An Exit The renewed enthusiasm surrounding Zcash has attracted a different kind of investor from the one buying ZEC in 2017. Corporate treasury strategies have emerged, institutional investors have taken an interest in privacy-focused assets, and the debate over financial surveillance has given Zcash a fresh investment narrative. NewsBTC previously reported that Winklevoss Capital backed the launch of a dedicated Zcash treasury strategy, illustrating how exposure to the cryptocurrency has begun extending beyond traditional crypto wallets. But the revival of an old cryptocurrency also comes with an interesting complication: investors who have spent years underwater finally have an opportunity to recover their capital or take profits. That does not necessarily make the Kraken deposit bearish. A transfer to an exchange is not proof of a completed sale, and one wallet cannot establish a broader trend among Zcash holders. Still, the transaction is worth watching. If more early investors start moving dormant coins onto exchanges, Zcash’s new buyers may find themselves absorbing supply from an entirely different generation of holders. Nine years ago, someone reportedly committed more than $5 million to the idea of private digital money. Today, the blockchain offers a glimpse of what that investment has become. Whether the owner has finished holding Zcash is a question the blockchain alone cannot yet answer.
content: A long-dormant Zcash whale recently moved 15,750 ZEC, valued at approximately $11.39 million, to Kraken after nine years. According to Lookonchain, the investor originally bought the coins in 2017 for an estimated $5 million. While the exchange deposit does not confirm an immediate sale, the transaction highlights how Zcash's recent market revival is providing early, long-term holders with an opportunity to realize significant gains.
content_ta: ஒன்பது ஆண்டுகளுக்குப் பிறகு, ஒரு செயலற்ற Zcash திமிங்கலம் தோராயமாக $11.39 மில்லியன் மதிப்புள்ள 15,750 ZEC நாணயங்களை Kraken பரிமாற்றத்திற்கு மாற்றியுள்ளது. title: Sale Edge and Neumetria offer AI agents and lenders a current, cross-bank view of customers
summary:
Neumetria, a behavioural understanding layer for financial platforms and AI agents, has partnered with Salt Edge, a leading open banking solutions provider, to serve clients in Europe and North America.
Salt Edge supplies consented, normalised account data from across a customer’s banks, while Neumetria turns that activity into a current, evidence-based view of the person behind it, covering income, liquidity, commitments, and financial capacity.
Together, they enable banks, lenders, fintechs, and teams building financial AI agents to get a clearer picture of each customer before they lend, engage or act, while each institution sets the rules and stays in control of every decision.  
From data to understanding 
Open banking has made account data much easier to access, but data alone doesn’t provide understanding. This makes it difficult to distinguish a temporary money spike from a lasting shift, or someone forming a new financial pattern from someone losing an established one. 
Two complementary layers
The key to understanding a customer’s financial activity doesn’t lie in one place. Income, spending, savings and credit commitments are spread across different accounts and institutions. Bringing them together consistently requires extensive connectivity infrastructure that is costly and complex to build and maintain in-house. 
With Salt Edge’s Data Aggregation, Neumetria builds on consistent, up-to-date account data from a single integration,  rather than connecting bank by bank. That frees Neumetria to focus on the next layer: providing institutions with insights for more informed risk evaluation, product recommendations and automated actions. Customers benefit too. Instead of uploading statements, they connect their accounts in a few clicks.
NoYesOpen Banking26 Nov, 2026
content: Salt Edge and Neumetria have partnered to provide financial institutions and AI agents with a comprehensive, cross-bank view of customer finances. By combining Salt Edge's open banking data aggregation with Neumetria's behavioural analysis, lenders and fintechs across Europe and North America can access real-time insights into customer income, liquidity, and financial capacity while maintaining full control over their decisions.

title: GITEX GLOBAL and Expand North Star to Be Hosted at Dubai Exhibition Centre, Expo City Dubai
summary:
Dubai is set to become the epicentre of an intensifying global conversation on the future AI economy next month, as tech leaders, policymakers, investors and innovators from more than 120 countries fill 46 sold-out halls at the world’s largest and most international tech and AI event of the year.
With more than 6,000 exhibitors and 10,000-plus tech brands on show, GITEX GLOBAL 2026 is moving ahead at full scale, arriving at a pivotal moment for the tech industry. AI is advancing at extraordinary speed, redefining economic power, national competitiveness and entire industries, yet competing perspectives are sharpening debates on AI sovereignty, regulation, responsible deployment and the future of intelligent infrastructure.
With a high-impact agenda built around ‘The Global Reset 2027 – Through a New Lens’, GITEX GLOBAL gives these questions a dedicated opening day at the inaugural GITEX SUMMIT on 7 December at Dubai World Trade Centre (DWTC). 
The 46th edition of the mega tech showcase then moves to Dubai Exhibition Centre (DEC), Expo City Dubai, the new home of GITEX GLOBAL (8-11 December) and Expand North Star (8-10 December), its powerhouse startup and investor connector event.
“AI is accelerating discovery and reshaping economies, while intensifying debates around trust, ethics, sovereignty, security, infrastructure and energy,” said Trixie LohMirmand, EVP of inD, the organiser of GITEX GLOBAL and Expand North Star. “GITEX GLOBAL 2026 captures this defining moment, bringing together competing perspectives to challenge assumptions, examine the strategic choices ahead and advance a shared commitment to responsible progress.”
The GITEX SUMMIT, a new lens on the year ahead
The GITEX SUMMIT is set to be the year’s most anticipated tech gathering for business networking, industry intelligence and knowledge exchange. Leaders will weigh the decisions defining the year ahead, from the compute economy and the new map of capital to the race to superintelligence, giving business executives the clarity to enter 2027 with re-energised foresight.
Headliners include Marc Ganzi, CEO of DigitalBridge, the digital infrastructure investor acquired by SoftBank in a US$3.1 billion deal completed in September; Nina Schick, GenAI expert and author of Deepfakes, the first book on AI-generated content, who has advised Joe Biden and Emmanuel Macron; Anne Neuberger, General Partner and Head of Global Affairs at Andreessen Horowitz and former White House cyber and emerging tech adviser; and Gary Marcus, Emeritus Professor at New York University, a leading advocate of neurosymbolic AI and a widely recognised critic of AI hype.
They lead a line-up of more than 500 expert speakers across the full five-day programme, with sessions ranging from AI market shocks and the rise of the agentic economy to the physical AI phenomenon and frontier breakthroughs in longevity and biosciences. 
Frontier AI powers new launches in robotics, compute and longevity
At DEC from 8-11 December, new showcases track where the AI economy moves next. GITEX Robotics & Mobility arrives as global humanoid shipments rise nearly 300 percent in the first half of 2026, featuring leading ‘embodied AI’ companies including agile quadruped and humanoid maker Unitree, service robot specialist Pudu Robotics and Walker S humanoid developer UBTECH.
The Robotics & Mobility Park presents US-based Joby Aviation’s electric air taxi, launching soon in Dubai with the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA), and Mercedes-Benz’s Level 4 robotaxi trials.
GITEX Super Data Centre tackles the US$7 trillion infrastructure build-out powering the AI race. GITEX RetailX targets a MENA retail market projected to reach US$1.4 trillion by 2032, and LIVX by GITEX connects AI with a longevity market projected to reach US$610 billion by 2030.
Unicorns valued at a combined US$76 billion also headline the show floor, led by Sweden’s Legora, the US$8.8 billion legal AI platform; VAST Data, which powers nine of the world’s top 10 frontier AI labs; and Switzerland’s Nexthink, a digital employee experience software provider that optimises 30 million endpoints across 1,300-plus enterprises worldwide.
Tech titans put trusted, resilient AI at the heart of the 2027 reset
As businesses reassess priorities and plans for the coming year, GITEX GLOBAL welcomes the biggest tech names redefining industries, and equipping businesses for the next phase of the AI economy. Heavyweights AWS, Etisalat, G42, Google, Huawei, IBM, Lenovo, Microsoft, and Oracle, return with a larger, more powerful presence in 2026, focusing on new commercial prospects, project launches and cross-border collaboration.

title: Maldives Islamic Bank Launches Visa Islamic Credit Card Proposition With BPC
summary:
