Built on the next-generation SmartVista platform, the initiative expands MIB’s retail payments offering while introducing a new financing proposition aligned with Islamic banking principles.
The launch opens a new avenue for growth for MIB and gives customers in the Maldives a modern alternative in the market. Structured around the Ujrah model the card allows customers to transact on credit and repay within an agreed period while remaining aligned with Islamic banking principles. Visa connectivity is available from launch, with Mastercard planned for a future phase, giving MIB a foundation to broaden its proposition over time.
Ahmed Riza, Deputy CEO, Maldives Islamic Bank, commented: “Launching our first Ujrah card is an important milestone in the development of MIB’s retail banking proposition and in our wider issuing modernisation journey. We have selected BPC for this project based on its existing SmartVista infrastructure and BPC’s experience supporting Islamic banking and card programmes across the region. Building on our long-standing partnership has given us the flexibility and technology foundation to bring this proposition to market and continue evolving it as customer needs develop.”
Leveraging the new platform, MIB now has end-to-end control over the lifecycle of its Ujrah card proposition, from application and account management through to transaction processing, billing, statements, rewards and reporting. The bank can configure card categories, limits, usage rules, currency restrictions and value propositions according to different customer segments, as well as support multiple products and supplementary cards with individually allocated limits.
The overall delivery model combines SmartVista capabilities deployed on-premise with card processing and Visa connectivity provided as a service. This hybrid approach allows MIB to build on its existing payments infrastructure while adding new issuing capabilities through a flexible and scalable service model.
The response to the new proposition has been immediate, with more than 500 applications received on the first day of launch, demonstrating strong customer interest in an Islamic credit card option and the growth potential MIB identified when entering the segment.
Subash Chandra Bowse, Country Director - Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and The Maldives, BPC, commented: “MIB has been a trusted partner for almost a decade, and this project represents an important new stage in that relationship. Our experience with Islamic banking and flexible card management technology allowed us to support MIB in building a credit card proposition designed specifically for its market and customers. We are honored to support MIB on its journey, powering its transformation with our SmartVista platform.”

title: AI Is Becoming Britain’s Financial Confidant, but Expert Warns: ‘Reassured Isn’t the Same as Well Advised’
summary:
AI is becoming a financial confidant for millions of Britons, providing a private, judgement-free space to ask money questions they feel uncomfortable discussing with another person, according to new research from wealth management platform Moneybox.  However, Moneybox is warning AI users that reassuring answers aren’t the same as accurate advice. 
An estimated 8.7 million Britons have already turned to AI with financial questions they wouldn't ask another person. Four in ten UK adults (41%) say they would rather admit to AI that they don't understand something about money than to a real person. Nearly two fifths (37%) would feel more comfortable being completely honest about their finances with AI, while 36% would be more likely to disclose a financial mistake to AI than another person.
This willingness to open up is particularly pronounced among younger adults. Among 25–34 year-olds, nearly three in five (58%) would rather admit financial confusion to AI, 60% feel more comfortable being completely honest about their finances, and 55% would be more likely to share a financial mistake.
While speed and convenience (35%) are the leading features that attract people to AI, more than a quarter (26%) value the ability to ask unlimited follow-up questions rising to two-thirds (67%) of 25–34-year-olds
Among AI users, 16% value researching an issue before deciding whether to speak to someone else, while 14% feel less embarrassed asking AI and 13% appreciate being able to ask questions without feeling judged.
Interestingly, just 9% of AI users cite trusting AI as an expert as a reason for using it. Almost one in five (19%) admitted to rephrasing a question until they received an answer they felt comfortable with. 
However, experts are keen to stress that reassurance alone does not guarantee that the information they receive is accurate or appropriate for their circumstances.
Brian Byrnes, Director of Personal Finance at Moneybox, said: “Feeling reassured isn't the same as being well advised. AI can sound convincing even when it's wrong. General-purpose AI tools aren't regulated financial advisers, don't necessarily have the full picture of someone's finances, goals and circumstances needed to make informed recommendations, and don't offer the same accountability or consumer protections as regulated providers.”
More than a third of UK adults (36%) say using AI makes them feel calmer or less anxious about financial decisions rising to 55% of 25–34-year-olds
Among people who have used AI for financial questions, almost a quarter have used it to double-check a decision they had already made (24%) or sought reassurance before taking action (23%).
Despite the concerns of being led astray, these findings highlight howAI can help people feel more confident about their money, and begin to improve financial confidence.
Brian Byrnes, Director of Personal Finance at Moneybox, said: “Money is still an uncomfortable subject for many people to discuss openly. AI has huge potential to break down the barriers that prevent people from engaging with their finances, helping them build the knowledge and confidence to take greater control of their financial futures earlier in life. Whether you're worried about debt, confused about investing or unsure how to plan for retirement, being able to ask questions privately, at your own pace and without fear of judgement can be incredibly empowering.
“The real opportunity is to turn greater financial confidence into better financial decisions. That means helping people understand how to use AI wisely to learn, research and explore their options, while recognising when to turn to regulated financial providers for personalised guidance or advice, backed by appropriate safeguards and consumer protections.”
5 practical steps to use AI wisely and make smarter money decisions
1. Get curious, not confused. Unsure about compound interest, ISAs or pensions? Ask AI to explain unfamiliar concepts in plain English, use everyday examples or break complicated topics into simple steps. If something doesn't make sense, ask it to explain it differently.
2. Explore your options, don't outsource your decisions. Use AI to research financial products, understand how they work and compare their benefits, risks, rules and providers. But don't rely on it for specific recommendations. General-purpose AI doesn't have the full picture of your finances needed to judge what's right for you.
3. Ask the questions you haven't thought of yet. Before making a financial decision, ask AI: "What might I be overlooking?", "What risks should I consider?" or "What questions should I ask my financial provider?" Use the answers to guide your research, not make your decision.
4. Sounds convincing? Check before you act. AI can sound authoritative even when its information is wrong or outdated. Always double-check important details, including interest rates, tax rules and product terms, with trusted sources such as MoneyHelper, GOV.UK or the provider itself. Never share passwords, account numbers or sensitive personal information.
5. Know when to bring in the experts. AI can help you build knowledge and explore your options, but understanding financial products isn't the same as knowing what's right for you. For personalised guidance or advice about savings, investments, pensions or mortgages, turn to an appropriately regulated provider that can consider your circumstances, with clear accountability and relevant consumer protections.

title: PEPE Whales Are Sitting On $21 Million In Tokens, And One Wallet Keeps Getting Bigger
summary: Key takeaways Lookonchain reports PEPE whales hold more than six trillion tokens, about $21.16 million, most of it in one wallet (0x5011) that has been buying since November 17. That wallet holds 5.15 trillion PEPE, roughly $18.28 million and about 1.22% of total supply; a second wallet (0x6246) holds 868.16 billion PEPE, about $2.88 million. Not all large holders agree: Deep Blue Alpha data shows withdrawals were only about 36% of tracked whale transfers over seven days, so exchange deposits outweighed them. Exchange deposits are not necessarily sales, and withdrawals do not prove a fresh purchase. At this size, exiting at the quoted price depends on liquidity; a $0.000001 price move changes a 5.15 trillion position by $5.15 million. PEPE whales have accumulated more than six trillion tokens worth approximately $21.16 million, according to new data from blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain. Most of that position belongs to a single unidentified wallet that has been accumulating the memecoin since November 17. The size of the position is unusual even by memecoin standards. One address now holds more than 1% of PEPE’s entire supply, and its owner has continued adding tokens despite weakness in the market. A Mystery PEPE Whale Keeps Adding To Its Position The wallet, identified by its opening characters 0x5011, accumulated 5.15 trillion PEPE over eight days. Lookonchain valued the holdings at $18.28 million, representing approximately 1.22% of the cryptocurrency’s total supply. The more interesting detail is how quickly the position has grown. Lookonchain’s transaction monitoring history shows that by November 19, the wallet had withdrawn around 1.9 trillion PEPE from Binance. That figure climbed to 2.878 trillion by November 23 and exceeded 3.3 trillion the following day. On Wednesday, Lookonchain reported that the address had accumulated 4.16 trillion tokens. By Thursday, its reported holdings had reached 5.15 trillion. Another wallet, beginning with 0x6246, accumulated 868.16 billion PEPE valued at approximately $2.88 million, bringing the combined reported value to more than $21 million. Large withdrawals are nothing new for the memecoin. NewsBTC previously covered a separate PEPE whale moving $14.7 million out of Binance. What makes the latest activity particularly interesting is the repeated accumulation within such a short period. The Other Side Of The PEPE Whale Trade Before treating these transactions as a bullish signal, it’s worth looking at what other large holders have been doing. Data from blockchain analytics platform Deep Blue Alpha showed that withdrawals accounted for approximately 36% of tracked PEPE whale transfers between wallets and exchanges over the preceding seven days, according to its November 26 update. In other words, exchange deposits outweighed withdrawals within that particular group of wallets. That doesn’t invalidate Lookonchain’s findings. It does, however, complicate the idea that large investors are collectively preparing for a PEPE recovery. One group of holders may be increasing its exposure while others are looking to reduce theirs. The distinction matters, especially in a market where a handful of transactions can attract more attention than the activity of dozens of other wallets. Exchange deposits aren’t necessarily sales, just as withdrawals don’t establish that a fresh purchase has taken place. Centralized exchange trading records remain largely invisible to outside observers. What A Trillion-Token Position Means For PEPE For an investor holding 5.15 trillion PEPE, even a movement of $0.000001 in the token’s price would change the value of the position by $5.15 million. That illustrates both the attraction and the risk of holding such a large quantity of a speculative asset. Building an $18 million position is one thing. Exiting it at the quoted market price is another. The amount an investor can actually realize depends on available liquidity, execution and the market’s ability to absorb the tokens. Concentrated holdings can therefore work in both directions. If tokens remain outside exchanges, they may reduce the supply immediately available for trading. If the same tokens return to exchanges, traders may suddenly find themselves watching for potential selling pressure. The next development worth following is whether these wallets continue accumulating or begin transferring tokens back to trading platforms. For now, two addresses hold an unusually large amount of PEPE. Whether the rest of the market shares their apparent appetite for the memecoin is a different question.
content: Lookonchain data reveals PEPE whales hold over six trillion tokens worth approximately $21.16 million. A single mystery wallet, 0x5011, accumulated 5.15 trillion PEPE since November 17, representing about 1.22% of the total supply. While this massive accumulation draws attention, other analytics show exchange deposits still outweigh withdrawals among certain large holders, complicating broader recovery signals for the memecoin.
content_ta: Lookonchain தரவுகளின்படி, PEPE வேல்ஸிடம் ஆறு டிரில்லியனுக்கும் அதிகமான டோக்கன்கள் சுமார் $21.16 மில்லியன் மதிப்பில் உள்ளன. நவம்பர் 17 முதல் ஒற்றை மர்ம வாலட் ஆன 0x5011, 5.15 டிரில்லியன் PEPE-ஐச் சேர்த்து மொத்த சப்ளையில் சுமார் 1.22% தன்வசம் வைத்துள்ளது. இந்த மிகப்பெரிய குவிப்பு கவனத்தை ஈர்த்தாலும், மற்ற பெரிய ஹோல்டர்களிடையே எக்ஸ்சேஞ்ச் டெபாசிட்டுகள் அதிகமாக உள்ளதாக பகுப்பாய்வுகள் காட்டுகின்றன.

title: Securing Trust in the Quantum Era: Why the Financial Industry Must Prepare Together
summary:
Quantum computing can still feel like a distant prospect. And that distance can make its opportunities and risks easy to underestimate.
Yet looking beyond the technology itself reveals a much more immediate question: how do we continue to protect trust as the foundations of digital security are about to be challenged?
Today’s financial system depends on trust. Trust that transactions are authentic, communications are secure and identities can be verified. For decades, that trust has rested on cryptographic techniques that are considered effectively unbreakable, provided they are regularly updated and strengthened over time.
Quantum computing – an emerging technology that aims to solve computational problems significantly faster than traditional computers – is challenging that assumption. It has the potential to overcome mathematical problems on which many of today’s widely used cryptographic algorithms rely.
In practical terms, that means the safeguards that protect confidentiality, integrity and authentication today could be defeated in the future. Over time, attackers could convincingly fake digital signatures that secure financial transactions or decrypt sensitive communications.
Preparing for the impact of quantum computing therefore requires decisive action across the financial ecosystem, including a transition from cryptographic methods that could become vulnerable to new, quantum-resistant standards.
That’s why post-quantum security readiness is a strategic priority at Swift. For nearly a decade, we have been actively preparing for this shift and helping shape the industry’s response to stay ahead of emerging risks and lead our community towards a quantum-ready future, preserving the security and trust on which global finance depends.
Quantum risk goes to the heart of whether the integrity of the financial system can continue to be trusted as technology evolves.





Understanding the scale of the shift
To understand why this preparation matters, let’s consider how quantum computing challenges the mechanisms that underpin trust in digital systems, including digital signatures, authentication and encryption.
For example, if digital signatures can be forged, attackers could impersonate trusted institutions without needing to steal private keys, no matter the strength of the key protection. If widely used key exchange mechanisms are broken, secure communication channels could be compromised.
And if encrypted data can be decrypted retrospectively, sensitive information intercepted today could be exposed in the future, a risk often described as ‘harvest now, decrypt later’. Similarly, digital signatures trusted today could potentially be forged in the future, undermining non-repudiation and disrupting the auditable chain of trust.
Quantum risk goes to the heart of whether the integrity of the financial system can continue to be trusted as technology evolves.
Building the financial community’s post-quantum future
The industry’s response is the development of post-quantum cryptography (PQC). These are new cryptographic algorithms designed to replace those that could be broken by quantum computing, while operating securely on today’s systems.
PQC algorithms deliver the same core functions as current cryptography, including key exchanges and digital signatures, but they rely on different mathematical foundations that are considered resistant to both classical and quantum attacks.
Standardisation is well underway, and the first set of quantum-resistant algorithms were finalised in 2024. Their adoption, however, is not a simple replacement exercise.
Today’s cryptography is deeply embedded across systems, applications and processes. Transitioning to new standards requires organisations to understand where they are exposed and manage change in a controlled and resilient way.
Rather than waiting for a complete inventory of cryptographic assets, organisations can prioritise their most critical and exposed systems and begin the PQC transition, while continuing to build a fuller view of their environment in parallel.
As the cryptographic landscape is expected to evolve more rapidly than in the past, greater cryptographic agility will help organisations adapt efficiently as standards evolve.
Why ecosystem readiness matters
Organisations are now at different stages of their PQC journey. Some have begun assessing their cryptographic exposure and experimenting with new algorithms. Others are at an earlier stage of awareness.
The challenge is not simply to migrate individual institutions to new cryptographic standards. It is ensuring that an interconnected financial ecosystem can transition securely and interoperably. That makes coordinated industry action critical.
At Swift, our experience demonstrates why early preparation matters. Post-quantum security readiness is a strategic priority, and for nearly a decade we have been monitoring developments in quantum computing and helping shape the industry’s response to emerging cryptographic risks.
Our preparations have progressed from assessing the impact of quantum risk and evaluating PQC to implementation activities aligned with emerging standards. Initial implementation activities are now underway, focusing on our core services.
Our experience also reinforces that customer readiness and interoperability have to be considered from the outset. Preparing our own infrastructure is just one part of the challenge.
Over the coming months, we will ramp up the delivery of our PQC capabilities to help our community make this shift, while maintaining the security, stability and interoperability on which financial communications depend.
Securing trust for the future
Quantum computing represents a fundamental shift in the technological landscape. While its full impact may still be years away, preparing an interconnected financial ecosystem for that change is essential.
Securing trust in the quantum era will require institutions to understand their exposure, plan their transition and coordinate with the wider ecosystem on which they depend.
By mobilising a coordinated transition today, we can collectively contribute to ensuring the foundations of financial trust endure into the quantum future.
Mike ManosChief Information OfficerSwiftYes
content: Quantum computing poses significant future risks to digital security in the financial industry, potentially breaking widely used cryptographic algorithms. To protect future transactions and sensitive communications, financial institutions must act together and transition to post-quantum cryptography standards. Swift is prioritizing this shift to ensure global financial stability and secure trust in the quantum era.

title: Japan weighs tighter oversight of DeFi, self-custodial wallets
summary: Japan’s financial regulator is exploring measures to curb illicit finance risks, including potential restrictions on access to DeFi services.
content: Japan's financial regulator is considering implementing stricter oversight measures for decentralized finance, known as DeFi, and self-custodial wallets. The initiative aims to address potential illicit finance risks and protect the broader financial ecosystem. Authorities are exploring various regulatory approaches to curb these risks, which may include restricting public access to certain DeFi services.

title: Monero’s Delisting Nightmare Continues: XMR Price Plunges 15%
summary: Key takeaways Monero fell about 15% on Thursday, from $525.36 to $446.54 per BitInfoCharts, after KuCoin announced it will delist XMR. KuCoin will end all four XMR spot pairs on November 30 at 08:00 UTC; deposits are already suspended and withdrawals stay open until December 31. XMR will also stop being accepted as collateral for VIP loans, so borrowers may need to add other collateral to avoid liquidation. KuCoin is the most active XMR venue (about $62.6 million in 24-hour volume on XMR/USDT per CoinGecko), following MEXC, Binance and Kraken EEA exits. The network does not depend on KuCoin, but liquidity does: watch where volume migrates and how much slippage the remaining exchanges show. Monero (XMR) lost around 15% of its value in less than five hours on Thursday after KuCoin announced plans to remove the privacy coin from its platform. The decision comes just nine days after rival exchange MEXC discontinued XMR spot trading, leaving investors with fewer options to trade one of the cryptocurrency market’s largest privacy-focused assets. Data from BitInfoCharts shows that Monero fell from $525.36 to $446.54 during Thursday’s trading session. For longtime XMR investors, the sell-off is an uncomfortable reminder of what happened when Binance announced its Monero delisting in February 2024. This time, however, the list of major exchanges available to Monero traders is considerably shorter. KuCoin Gives Monero Traders Four Days Before Trading Ends In a November 26 announcement, KuCoin confirmed that it will remove all four Monero spot trading pairs against USDT, USDC, ETH and BTC on November 30 at 08:00 UTC. The exchange has already suspended XMR deposits and does not intend to reopen them. Withdrawals are scheduled to remain available until December 31 at 08:00 UTC, although KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier if problems affecting the network arise. Monero’s removal extends beyond spot trading. KuCoin will discontinue XMR flexible savings on November 27, followed by its conversion and automated trading services on November 30. There is another detail in the announcement that deserves particular attention. KuCoin will stop accepting XMR as collateral for its VIP loan products. Customers who have borrowed against their Monero holdings may need to provide alternative collateral to avoid liquidation. For holders planning to leave their coins on the exchange until the withdrawal deadline, KuCoin also warned that remaining balances could be converted into stablecoins, although “such conversion is not guaranteed.” The exchange cited its platform policies but did not identify a specific regulatory requirement behind the decision. Monero’s Liquidity Problem Is Getting Harder To Ignore KuCoin is not the first exchange to abandon Monero this month, but its departure could prove particularly significant given the amount of XMR trading it handles. A November 26 snapshot from CoinGecko identified KuCoin as Monero’s most active exchange, with its XMR/USDT pair recording approximately $62.6 million in trading volume over a 24-hour period. Earlier this month, MEXC discontinued spot trading for Monero on November 17. Binance removed the cryptocurrency in February 2024, while Kraken halted XMR trading for European Economic Area customers in October of the same year, explicitly citing regulatory changes. Kaiko’s historical research illustrates how liquidity across privacy cryptocurrencies had already deteriorated by early 2024, following a series of exchange restrictions. Trading volume does not simply disappear when an exchange delists an asset. Some of it will move elsewhere, and investors who intend to keep their holdings can withdraw them to private wallets. The bigger question is how efficiently the remaining exchanges can absorb that activity. If fewer venues are competing for the same orders, particularly during periods of market stress, large trades could become more expensive to execute and price swings more pronounced. For Monero, that is increasingly a market structure problem rather than a question of whether its underlying technology works. Can XMR Survive Another Major Exchange Exit? There is a case against assuming that Thursday’s sell-off marks the beginning of a prolonged decline. Monero has survived previous exchange removals and even managed to establish new price highs in 2026 despite mounting restrictions. As NewsBTC previously reported, XMR traded above $700 earlier this year, long after Binance stopped supporting its spot markets. The cryptocurrency’s network does not depend on KuCoin to process transactions. Its utility as a privacy-focused payment system remains separate from its availability on centralized trading platforms. But a functioning network does not guarantee a liquid market. Investors still need practical ways to enter and exit their positions without incurring excessive trading costs. November 30 will therefore be an important test for Monero. Rather than focusing solely on whether XMR recovers the $500 level, traders should watch where KuCoin’s trading volume migrates and whether the remaining exchanges can absorb larger orders without substantial slippage. That will offer a better indication of whether Thursday’s decline was a temporary reaction to another delisting or a warning of a deeper liquidity problem.
content: Monero’s price plunged about 15% after KuCoin announced it will delist XMR and end all spot trading pairs on November 30. Deposits are suspended and withdrawals remain open until December 31. KuCoin is the most active exchange for XMR, following recent exits by MEXC, Binance, and Kraken. The move raises concerns over shrinking market liquidity and fewer trading options for privacy coin investors.

title: Coinbase Issues December Alert: Key Services to Face Temporary Disruptions
summary: Is there any cause for alarm?

title: Bitcoin Miners Go 98 Minutes Without Finding a Single Block
summary: Bitcoin miners went 98 minutes and 19 seconds without finding a block on Nov. 26, the longest gap since July.

This unusual gap in transaction processing is recorded as the longest period without a block discovery since July, drawing attention from the cryptocurrency community regarding network mining activity and block generation times.
